label: late original-phase input of a k/a/t/r/o/y/m/w/j/e-type letter
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, and never at t<3, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase. The firing rate climbs with position: 3% at t=3, 15% at t=6-7, 55% at orig_idx 8. It peaks on the last one or two inputs before <DEL> (to_go=0 holds 47% of the mass) and is therefore stronger in longer sequences. Within that window it depends strongly on the current input letter. k, a, t, r, o, y, m and w are best (13-17% rate), j and e are moderate, and g, c and most digits are weak. First occurrences of a token fire more (in_first holds 82% of the mass). It also depends on earlier context: sequences whose first token is w, q, v, l, d, g, i or b push precision to about 0.8. This looks like a graded sum of position, current token and history, so a boolean predicate only captures most of the mass. The top activations are the final 1-2 original steps of length-8/9 sequences with letters like k/a/r/t.
